paper.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
paper.abstract: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present \textbf{GRSE}, \textbf{G}roup-\textbf{R}elative \textbf{S}kill \textbf{E}volution, which assigns behavioral credit by comparison: inspired by GRPO, it executes each question several times under the same skill libraries and contrasts the executions to credit agent--skill pairs, with structured diagnosis of failures. On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ($+6.7$ and $+3.2$ F1). Its gains rest on better-grounded retrieval rather than answers given without evidence, and its learned skills transfer between the multi-hop tasks. GRSE is robust to corrupted libraries: starting from planted harmful skills, it credits every planted skill with the correct sign and recovers the score of a clean library ($+6.3$ points), whereas MASkills misattributes two and falls below its starting point.

one_sentence.text: GRSE针对团队奖励难以归因到具体技能的问题，通过同题多次执行对比、结构化诊断和验证门控更新技能；作者报告其在HotpotQA及LoCoMo非开放域类别优于MASkills，LoCoMo多跳F1分别提升6.7和3.2。

evidence.quote: GRSE executes each question several times under the same skill libraries, compares the executions agent by agent, and attributes the team’s outcome to individual agent–skill pairs. Structured diagnosis grounds each attribution in checked execution steps, and the resulting credit drives targeted, validated skill updates.

On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ( +6.7 and +3.2 F1).

research_problem.text: 作者指出，技能在成功轨迹中出现不等于促成成功；按出现情况分配信用，可能奖励实际有害的技能。

evidence.quote: Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit.

research_problem.text: 研究目标是在模型参数固定的协作团队中，将团队结果归因到智能体及其自然语言技能，支持针对性的技能更新。

evidence.quote: We studied behavioral credit assignment in cooperative language-model teams whose agents keep fixed parameters and act through natural-language skills. GRSE executes each question several times under the same skill libraries, compares the executions agent by agent, and attributes the team’s outcome to individual agent–skill pairs.

The critic receives both absolute rewards r_{qg} and relative advantages A_{qg} to compare trajectories and draws on execution evidence to assess skill credit (§ 3.2 ). Groups with equal-reward carry no contrasts but still show which behaviors consistently fail or succeed, so they are kept by default.

method_steps.text: 评论器逐智能体比较执行，标注技能有益、冗余、有害或中性；结构化诊断核查引用步骤、智能体归属与编辑资格，工具故障或责任不明时不编辑，违规诊断退回修复一次。

evidence.quote: The critic reads all G executions of a question together and compares them agent by agent.
v labels the skill as helped, redundant, harmful, or neutral; e gives supporting evidence; and \Delta suggests a refinement.

The critic interface checks that step references exist, match the named agent, and cite non-full-reward executions for L^{-} and full-reward executions for L^{+} . Refinement additionally requires an owned skill recorded in the cited failed rollout and a matching credit.
Tool failures and uncertain or unknown responsibility permit only no edit.
Diagnoses that violate the constraints are returned to the critic once for repair.

method_steps.text: 跨题汇总信用后修订、剪枝、合并或新增技能；每个候选库单独替换到更新前团队，验证分数不低于原分数减δ才接受，全部测试后组合获准候选。

evidence.quote: We therefore aggregate credit across questions into edit direction for existing skills and evidence for new skills.
The operators refine credited skills along \Gamma_{i} , prune skills with low utility, consolidate redundant ones, and induce new skills from E_{i} .

author_contributions.text: 作者自述沿用MASkills的技能表示与编辑算子，贡献集中于同题执行比较，以及将失败连接到智能体、技能、步骤引用和受检查编辑动作的结构化诊断。

evidence.quote: We retain its skill representation and editing operators and change how credit is formed: GRSE jointly compares same-question team executions, and structured diagnosis links each failure to an agent–skill target, cited execution steps, and a checked edit action.

author_contributions.text: 作者将检索改善、多跳任务间技能迁移及污染技能库修复作为方法有效性的证据；这些机制解释属于作者主张。

evidence.quote: Table 3: Answer transitions from the empty to the final library.
All rows use the first run of each method; on LoCoMo, each category has its own library, and empty-library answers come from iteration 0 of the same GRSE run.
With the Gemma4 actor on LoCoMo, declined questions that become correct account for most of GRSE’s gain ( +6.0 of +7.4 ), and the last two columns show how they are fixed.

MASkills reduces declines without improving retrieval: the share of questions with no cited evidence stays at 22%, and 9 of its 34 D \to C lack evidence. GRSE lowers this share to 14%, with only 5 of 61 lacking evidence, consistent with crediting Agent 1’s search rather than Agent 2’s answer.
Otherwise it is correct if its F1 score is at least 0.5 and wrong if not.

On LoCoMo, a question has evidence if the retriever’s output cites at least one dialogue turn ( [D session : turn ] ). Outputs that say NO_EVIDENCE , print a grep call instead of running it, or return nothing usable count as no evidence.
All analyses use the first run of each configuration and greedy decoding.

limitations.text: 作者明确限定评估范围为两个问答基准、两种actor、一个critic和双智能体顺序团队；更大团队、非顺序通信、长程工具任务及其他critic尚待测试。

evidence.quote: we evaluate two-agent sequential teams on two question-answering benchmarks with two open-weight actors and one critic model. Larger teams, non-sequential communication, longer tool-heavy tasks, and other critic models remain to be tested in the future.

roles.text: 两个智能体角色固定：HotpotQA中Agent 1读取问题及篇章，Agent 2结合其响应给出最终答案；LoCoMo中Agent 1检索，Agent 2仅据检索证据作答。

evidence.quote: Roles do not change during training. On HotpotQA (Figure 7 ), the two agents act in sequence: Agent 1 sees the question and passages, and Agent 2 additionally sees Agent 1’s response and gives the final answer.
On LoCoMo (Figures 8 and 9 ), Agent 1 searches the conversation with <grep> calls (at most three, each returning up to 20 matching turns), and Agent 2 answers from the retrieved evidence only.

evidence.quote: We studied behavioral credit assignment in cooperative language-model teams whose agents keep fixed parameters and act through natural-language skills.

update_method.text: 每轮修订和归纳，每两轮合并；HotpotQA每两轮、LoCoMo每三轮剪枝。现有技能采用锚定编辑，新技能从归纳证据创建。

evidence.quote: The operator schedule \Omega applies refinement and induction every iteration, consolidation every second iteration, and pruning every second (HotpotQA) or third (LoCoMo) iteration.
Induction creates a new skill from the induction evidence collected for an agent, refinement applies anchored edits to an existing skill, and consolidation merges overlapping skills (Figure 13 ).

system_insights: 系统分析：同题对比和引用检查提供可审计的归因路径，但不足以证明因果责任；作者也将解释限定为观察性判断（b00020、b00025）。
系统分析：各候选分别在旧团队中获准，不能保证组合后的性能不降；δ还允许单项验证分数小幅下降（b00036—b00038）。
系统分析：主比较同时涉及轨迹数量、LoCoMo训练解码和训练成本差异，不能仅凭主结果隔离信用算法本身的净收益（b00041、b00079、b00108）。

evidence.quote: GRSE executes each question several times under the same skill libraries, compares the executions agent by agent, and attributes the team’s outcome to individual agent–skill pairs. Structured diagnosis grounds each attribution in checked execution steps, and the resulting credit drives targeted, validated skill updates.

On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ( +6.7 and +3.2 F1).
Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit.

We studied behavioral credit assignment in cooperative language-model teams whose agents keep fixed parameters and act through natural-language skills. GRSE executes each question several times under the same skill libraries, compares the executions agent by agent, and attributes the team’s outcome to individual agent–skill pairs.

We set G=4 consistently in our experiments.

The critic receives both absolute rewards r_{qg} and relative advantages A_{qg} to compare trajectories and draws on execution evidence to assess skill credit (§ 3.2 ). Groups with equal-reward carry no contrasts but still show which behaviors consistently fail or succeed, so they are kept by default.
The critic reads all G executions of a question together and compares them agent by agent.
v labels the skill as helped, redundant, harmful, or neutral; e gives supporting evidence; and \Delta suggests a refinement.

The critic interface checks that step references exist, match the named agent, and cite non-full-reward executions for L^{-} and full-reward executions for L^{+} . Refinement additionally requires an owned skill recorded in the cited failed rollout and a matching credit.
Tool failures and uncertain or unknown responsibility permit only no edit.
Diagnoses that violate the constraints are returned to the critic once for repair.
We therefore aggregate credit across questions into edit direction for existing skills and evidence for new skills.
The operators refine credited skills along \Gamma_{i} , prune skills with low utility, consolidate redundant ones, and induce new skills from E_{i} .

Accepted candidates are assembled after all agents are tested, and acceptance remains per agent.

We retain its skill representation and editing operators and change how credit is formed: GRSE jointly compares same-question team executions, and structured diagnosis links each failure to an agent–skill target, cited execution steps, and a checked edit action.
Its gains rest on better-grounded retrieval rather than answers given without evidence, and its learned skills transfer between the multi-hop tasks.

GRSE is robust to corrupted libraries: starting from planted harmful skills, it credits every planted skill with the correct sign and recovers the score of a clean library ( +6.3 points), whereas MASkills misattributes two and falls below its starting point.

evidence.section: Where do the gains come from?

evidence.quote: MASkills reduces declines without improving retrieval: the share of questions with no cited evidence stays at 22%, and 9 of its 34 D \to C lack evidence. GRSE lowers this share to 14%, with only 5 of 61 lacking evidence, consistent with crediting Agent 1’s search rather than Agent 2’s answer.
